rationale: The hypothesis posits that gait ataxia, peripheral sensory-motor neuropathy, and hypotonia are present in a majority of pediatric and juvenile cases (estimated at 70-85%). However, a systematic literature review of 44 reported patients with FDXR mutations by Masnada et al. (2023) established that sensorimotor peripheral polyneuropathy occurred in only 22.72% (10/44) and ataxia in 43.18% (19/44) of cases, directly refuting the 70-85% majority claim for neuropathy and ataxia. While hypotonia and optic atrophy (89% in Kaler and Couser 2025) are indeed frequent, sensory-motor polyneuropathy and gait ataxia are present in less than half of reported individuals.

evidence.text: A comprehensive literature review of 44 reported patients harboring FDXR mutations revealed an incidence of sensorimotor peripheral polyneuropathy of 22.72% and ataxia of 43.18%, demonstrating that neither finding reaches majority prevalence (70-85%) across the clinical cohort.

source.title: FDXR-associated disease: a challenging differential diagnosis with inflammatory peripheral neuropathy
source.quote: The review of clinical findings in previously described cases from literature reveals also a significant incidence of sensorimotor peripheral polyneuropathy (22.72%) and ataxia (43.18%). To date, 44 patients with FDXR mutations have been reported.

evidence.text: Review of 47 reported patients with FDXR variants shows that optic atrophy is the hallmark feature (89%), alongside movement disorders, sensorineural hearing loss, developmental delay/regression, and hypotonia, whereas peripheral polyneuropathy is not a predominant majority feature.

source.title: Ocular and neurological manifestations of the FDXR-related disorder
source.quote: Optic atrophy is the most common feature (89%), but many other ocular manifestations have not previously been characterized... Common neurological symptoms include movement disorder, sensorineural hearing loss, developmental delay/regression, and hypotonia.

evidence.text: FDXR deficiency spans a broad spectrum from severe infantile Leigh-like encephalopathy with early demise to milder movement disorders, with variable presence of hypotonia, spasticity, and cerebellar signs.

source.title: Expanding the clinical and genetic spectrum of FDXR deficiency by functional validation of variants of uncertain significance
source.quote: These patients show a broad clinical spectrum ranging from Leigh syndrome with early demise and severe infantile-onset encephalopathy, to milder movement disorders.

conflicts: The hypothesis estimates gait ataxia and peripheral sensory-motor neuropathy to occur in 70-85% of cases, directly conflicting with systematic review findings showing peripheral polyneuropathy in only 22.72% (10/44) and ataxia in 43.18% (19/44).

new_directions.question_text: What is the true prevalence and age-stratified penetrance of sensorimotor peripheral polyneuropathy in FDXR-associated disease across different variant categories (e.g., p.R392W vs p.R306C)?
new_directions.rationale: Given that peripheral neuropathy is present in under 25% of all reported cases but can present acutely and mimic Guillain-Barre syndrome, genotype-phenotype correlations could clarify which subcohorts are at risk.

new_directions.question_text: Does subclinical peripheral neuropathy or subclinical dorsal column dysfunction exist in asymptomatic or purely optic-atrophy-presenting FDXR individuals when evaluated by systematic nerve conduction studies?
new_directions.rationale: Neurophysiological testing may reveal under-reported peripheral nerve involvement that does not meet overt clinical diagnostic thresholds.
